rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nūn near ṣād is not pronounced clearly because both use the tongue tip; nūn in Yā Sīn and Nūn is clear because wāw is articulated at the lips.
rows.anchor: هذه النونات لا تبين في القراءة في قراءة أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite noun immediately negated by lā is accusative without tanwīn; lā acts like a verb, its predicate is nominative, and the noun is built as one unit with lā.
rows.anchor: وذلك ان كل اسم منكور نفيته ب"لا" وجعلت "لا" الى جنب الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For lā khawfun, rafʿ is the proper form because the coordinated phrase must also be nominative.
rows.anchor: فالوجه فيه الرفع لان المعطوف عليه لا يكون الا رفعا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some readers instead put khawf in the accusative and parse the following clause as a new nominal sentence.
rows.anchor: وقد قرأها قوم نصبا وجعلوا الآخر [رفعا] على الابتداء

rows.speaker: بعض القراء
rows.claim: Some readers assimilate the first hāʾ in fīhi into the hāʾ of hudā because identical consonants meet.
rows.anchor: قد قرأ بعض القراء {فيه هدى} فادغم الهاء الأولى

rows.speaker: العرب
rows.claim: Some Arabs treat hudā as feminine.
rows.anchor: وزعموا ان من العرب من يؤنث "الهدى"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Arabs silence the masculine pronominal hāʾ; the cited line, a usage said to be common among Asad al-Sarāt, has silent hāʾ in lahu.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يسكن هاء الاضمار للمذكر قال الشاعر: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد التاسع] : فظلت لدى البيت العتيق أخيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the pronoun ending in wa-mimmā razaqnāhum, some pause on it even in connected speech while others append wāw; several dialectal forms occur after a preceding kasra or yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قوله {ومما رزقناهم ينفقون} ففيها لغتان

rows.speaker: العرب
rows.claim: After a kasra or still yāʾ, speakers vary the hāʾ and mīm vowels and may append yāʾ or wāw; other forms leave the mīm paused.
rows.anchor: فمن العرب من يقول: "عليهمي" فيلحق الياء ويكسر الميم والهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final consonant rendered still at pause is treated like a preceding still yāʾ when the prior vowel is kasra.
rows.anchor: كل هذا اذا وقفت عليه فآخره ساكن والذي قبله مكسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Applying the same alternation to kum after a kasra or still yāʾ is rare and considered inelegant, but is a Bakr b. Wāʾil dialect with forms like ʿalaykumi and bikumi.
rows.anchor: وهي لغة لبكر بن وائل سمعناها من بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line the author says he heard from Bakr b. Wāʾil is cited as evidence for the dialectal pronoun behavior; the poet is unnamed.
rows.anchor: وإن قال مولاهم على جل حاجة * من الأمر ردوا فضل أحلامكم ردوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before a following still consonant, a wāw or yāʾ is deleted and the mīm is given the corresponding ḍamma or kasra.
rows.anchor: وكل هذا اذا لقيه حرف ساكن حركت الميم بالضم ان كان بعدها واو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same suffix-vowel treatment applies to the masculine singular hāʾ, as in passing by him or seeing him today.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الهاء التي للواحد المذكر من نحو "مررت به اليوم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some assimilate the two bāʾs in la-dhahaba bi-samʿihim, making the first sākin; others pronounce it with a vowel.
rows.anchor: فمنهم من يدغم ويسكن الباء الأولى لانهما حرفان مثلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samʿ is singular in form but may denote a collective, as in the cited Qurʾanic uses of hearing, sight, soul, and back.
rows.anchor: وجعل "السمع" في لفظ واحد وهو جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial alif is hamzat qaṭʿ because it remains in the diminutive form anīdād; the singular of andād is nidd, meaning an equal or counterpart.
rows.anchor: فقطع الالف لانه اسم تثبت الالف فيه في التصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase li-man ittaqā is elliptical: after stating the concession, the sense is that this concession is for whoever is God-fearing.
rows.anchor: كأنه حين ذكر هذه الرخصة قد أخبر عن أمر

words: وَيُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِي قَلْبِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first construal has the person himself call God to witness what is in his heart.
rows.anchor: قال {ويشهد الله على ما فى قلبه} اذا كان هو يشهد

words: وَيُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِي قَلْبِهِ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another construal makes God the one who witnesses what is in the person's heart.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {ويشهد الله} أي إن الله هو الذي يشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aladd is the intensive form from l-d-d, with the paradigms ladadtu/taluddu, a people called ludd, a woman laddāʾ, and women lud.
rows.anchor: من "لددت" "تلد" و"هو ألد" و"هم قوم لد"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharā can mean either sold or bought; the same two-way usage appears in jill and jalal for excellent/great or poor/small, and in sudf for darkness or light.
rows.anchor: قال {ومن الناس من يشري نفسه ابتغآء مرضات الله} يقول: "يبيعها"

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses jalal for a great calamity in the phrase رزء ذو جلل.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: [من الرمل وهو الشاهد الثامن والثلاثون بعد المئة] : وأرى أربد قد فارقني

rows.speaker: الآخر
rows.claim: A second unnamed poet uses jalal for something small: what follows the day at Jurthum is insignificant.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخر: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد التاسع والثلاثون بعد المئة] : ألا إنما أبكي ليوم لقيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtighāʾ is accusative under yashrī, as though preceded by li-; deleting the lām lets the verb govern it, as in the cited poem.
rows.anchor: واما قوله {ابتغآء مرضات الله} فان انتصابه على الفعل وهو على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurūʾ is prolonged and hamzated, singular qurʾ is lightly hamzated, and aqraʾa al-marʾa means she became menstruating; the form also describes having had one or two periods.
rows.anchor: قال {ثلاثة قروء} ممدودة مهموزة وواحدها "القرء" خفيفة مهموزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qurʾ is the cessation of menstruation.
rows.anchor: و"القرء": انقطاع الحيض. وقال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some instead define a qurʾ as the interval between two menstruations.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: "ما بين الحيضتين

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses qaraʾa janīnan for not conceiving, supporting the root's pregnancy-related usage.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر: [من الوافر وهو الشاهد الثالث والاربعون بعد المئة] : [76ء] ذراعي بكرة أدماء بكر * هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A second unnamed poet uses al-maqrāh for a watercourse, without hamza; it is unrelated to qurʾ in this sense.
rows.anchor: فان "المقراة": المسيل وليس بمهموز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw in wa-lā tansawū is kasra to resolve two successive still letters, as in ishtaraw al-ḍalāla.
rows.anchor: فكسر الواو لاجتماع الساكنين كما قال {اشتروا الضلالة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In fear, pray on foot or pray mounted.
rows.anchor: قال {فإن خفتم فرجالا أو ركبانا} يقول: "صلوا رجالا أو صلوا ركبانا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax is effectively li-azwājihim waṣiyyatan; the accusative matāʿan is understood as an instruction to provide them enjoyment.
rows.anchor: ونصب {متاعا} لانه حين قال {لأزواجهم} {وصية} فكأنه قد قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayra ikhrāj means without expulsion: provide enjoyment through the year, but do not expel them.
rows.anchor: فعلى هذا انتصب قوله {متاعا إلى الحول غير إخراج} يقول "لا إخراجا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They report that Ibn Masʿūd's codex read kataba ʿalaykum waṣiyyatan li-azwājikum.
rows.anchor: وزعموا أنها في حرف ابن مسعود {كتب عليكم وصية لأزواجكم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhfash reports the forms with Zakariyyā and Zakariyyāʾ as two dialects and says his reading is Zakariyyā without hamza.
rows.anchor: {وكفلها زكرياء} و {كفلها} ايضا {زكريا} وبه نقرأ وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read the verb with kasra on fāʾ in the form associated with Zakariyyāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم {وكفلها زكرياء} بكسر الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes differing vocalizations of kafala and their corresponding imperfects; one cited form kafila is one he has not heard himself.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: "كفل" قال "يكفل" ومن قال "كفل" [قال] "يكفل"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq without reckoning is like eating without strict account: provision is not counted out narrowly or restricted.
rows.anchor: فهذا مثل كلام العرب "يأكل بغير حساب" أي: لا يتعصب عليه ولا يضيق عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descriptions quick at reckoning and quickest of reckoners mean that the accounting involves no thought, deliberation, or recollection.
rows.anchor: و {سريع الحساب} و {أسرع الحاسبين} يقول: "ليس في حسابه فكر ولا روية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qad balaghanī al-kibar is like qad balaghanī al-jahd: I have reached old age or hardship, meaning I am in that state.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى {وقد بلغني الكبر} كما تقول "وقد بلغني الجهد"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illā ramzan is an exception from the initial clause: he was not to speak to people except by gesture; ramz means signaling.
rows.anchor: قال {ثلاثة أيام إلا رمزا} يريد: "أن لا تكلم الناس إلا رمزا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle idh in the account of the angels speaking to Mary has no expressed predicate.
rows.anchor: قال {وإذ قالت الملائكة يامريم} ف"إذ" ها هنا ليس له خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative ayyuhum follows because a search for knowledge can be followed by a question, as in the cited purpose clauses linalama and liyabluwakum.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى {إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم} لأن كل ما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In thumma lananziʿanna ... ayyuhum, ayyuhum is fixed on ḍamm, not inflected, because lananziʿanna is not a request for knowledge.
rows.anchor: فلم يرتفع على مثل ما ارتفع عليه الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He attaches ashadda to ayy as its complement; some put it in the accusative, which he says is analogical.
rows.anchor: وجعل {أشد} من صلتها وقد نصبها قوم وهو قياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read nominative aḥsanu as a relative-clause complement of alladhī; the accusative aḥsana makes it governed by the verb.
rows.anchor: وقد قرىء {تماما على الذي أحسن} فرفعوا وجعلوه من صلة "الذي"

rows.speaker: بعض العرب
rows.claim: Some Arabs say mā anā bi-lladhī qāʾilun laka shayʾan; in the dual they use bi-lladhayni qāʾilāni.
rows.anchor: وزعموا ان بعض العرب قال: "ما أنا بالذي قائل لك شيئا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza of nabaʾ is retained because it derives from anbaʾtuhu; the alif of ibn drops as a hamzat waṣl, and in pause nabaʾ is shortened rather than made nabā because it is annexed.
rows.anchor: فالهمزة ل"نبأ" لأنها من "أنباته". وألف "ابني" تذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When stopping on nabaʾ, he says to shorten the form, not say nabā, since it is in an annexation construction.
rows.anchor: واذا وقفت [قلت] "نبأ" مقصور ولا تقول "نبا" لأنها مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭawwaʿat means made easy or permissible; ṭawwaqtuhu amrī means I bound him to my affair.
rows.anchor: وقال {فطوعت له نفسه} مثل "فطوعت" ومعناه: "رخصت"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-uwaariya is accusative because it is coordinated by faʾ with an; it has no hamza because it derives from wāraytu.
rows.anchor: وقال {أعجزت أن أكون مثل هذاالغراب فأواري} فنصب {فأواري}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjaztu is from ʿajaza yaʿjizu; other speakers also use ʿajiza yaʿjazu or ʿajiza yaʿjizu.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم "عجز" "يعجز"، و"عجز" "يعجز"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma may mean waw here; alternatively the plural address is directed to Adam, as when a group is told they were struck though only their chief was struck.
rows.anchor: وقال {ثم صورناكم ثم قلنا للملائكة} لأن "ثم" في معنى الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā manaʿaka allā tasjuda means mā manaʿaka an tasjuda; lā is an extra particle joining the speech, as the poem demonstrates.
rows.anchor: وقال {ما منعك ألا تسجد} ومعناه: ما منعك أن تسجد، و {لا} ها هنا زائدة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line is explained by Arabs as abā jawduhu al-bukhla, with lā as an extra connective filler.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد الرابع بعد المئتين] : أبى جوده "لا" البخل

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yūnus reports that Abū ʿAmr read al-bukhli in the genitive, construing lā as the particle meaning no, which can signal either generosity or miserliness.
rows.anchor: وزعم يونس ان أبا عمرو كان يجر "البخل"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa lahumā means waswasa ilayhimā; Arabic verbs can take varied prepositions, as ghariḍtu can mean I longed for him, literally from these toward him.
rows.anchor: وقال {فوسوس لهما الشيطان} والمعنى: فوسوس اليهما الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception means he forbade them only out of aversion to their becoming angels, like the idiom iyyāka an tafʿala for fear or dislike of doing something.
rows.anchor: وقال {إلا أن تكونا ملكين} يقول: {ما نهاكما إلا} كراهة {أن تكونا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two vocalizations of ṭafiqa are reported, each with its matching imperfect form yaṭfaqu or yaṭfiqu.
rows.anchor: وقال {وطفقا} وقال بعضهم {وطفقا} فمن قال: "طفق" قال: "يطفق"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yakhṣifān derives from yakhtaṣifān, with tāʾ assimilated into ṣād; the resulting consonant cluster gives kasra to khāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال {يخصفان} جعلها من "يختصفان" فادغم التاء في الصاد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some open khāʾ by transferring the tāʾ's vowel onto it, as in the readings cited for yahdī.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يفتح الخاء ويحول عليها حركة التاء وهو كقوله {أمن لا يهدي}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He knows no reader who does not put dūna in the accusative.
rows.anchor: لا نعلم أحدا يقرؤها إلا نصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalf may mean any generation after a prior one, whether a replacement or not; khalaf can mean a substitute that takes the predecessor's place and fills its role.
rows.anchor: و"الخلف" الذي هو بدل مما كان قبله قد قام مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAraḍ is property other than dirhams and dinars, which are ʿayn; more broadly it is anything that comes across a person, including trouble or opportunity.
rows.anchor: وقال {يأخذون عرض هذاالأدنى} فأضاف "العرض" إلى "هذا" وفسر "هذا" ب"الأدنى"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related expressions ʿaraḍa lahu and aʿraḍa laka describe something coming across one's path; the cited poem uses muʿriḍan for facing the spears.
rows.anchor: وتقول: "أعرض لك الخير" و"عرض لك الخير"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿāriḍ of a cloud is what faces you; the passage also says al-ḥabī is what comes from every direction.
rows.anchor: و"العارض" من السحاب: ما استقبلك وهو قول الله عز وجل {فلما رأوه عارضا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ʿarḍ al-nās means what is toward you, as in ḍrib bihi ʿarḍ al-ḥāʾiṭ.
rows.anchor: وأما "الحبي": فما كان من كل ناحية وتقول: "خذوه من عرض الناس"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dimension term ʿarḍ, paired with ṭūl, is still-voweled; other uses include the verbal noun ʿarḍan for presenting a house or an affair appearing.
rows.anchor: وأما "العرض" و"الطول" فانه ساكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs ʿaraḍa and aʿraḍa are explained through the verbal noun ʿarḍan, including presenting a house or an affair appearing.
rows.anchor: و: "عرضت عليه المنزل عرضا" و"عرض لي أمر عرضا" هذا مصدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line he cites uses ʿaraḍū al-khaṭṭī; he explains ʿaraḍū and aʿraḍū from the root ʿaraḍa.
rows.anchor: إذا عرضوا الخطي فوق الكواثب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What comes across a person of worldly good can be a benefit; ʿaraḍ min al-khayr wa-l-sharr describes what one encounters and profits from, with bad occurrences also named.
rows.anchor: و"العرض من الخير والشر": ما أصبت عرضا من الدنيا فانتفعت به

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read al-anṣāru nominative, coordinating with al-sābiqūn; Akhfash prefers the genitive because the earliest forerunners were from both groups.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم (والأنصار) رفع عطفه على قوله (والسابقون) والوجه هو الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction can omit bi- before the second object, as in khalatū bi-ākhar, like istawā al-māʾ wa-l-khashabata meaning with the timber.
rows.anchor: فيجوز في العربية ان تكون "بآخر" كما تقول: "استوى الماء والخشبة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-tuzakkīhim bihā may start an independent clause, or describe ṣadaqa and then be repeated as emphasis; the same analysis is allowed for tuṭahhiruhum.
rows.anchor: فقوله {وتزكيهم بها} على الابتداء وان شئت جعلته من صفة الصدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āyatan is accusative as the predicate of a definite noun.
rows.anchor: وقال {هاذه ناقة الله لكم آية} نصب على خبر المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In min khizyi yawmiʾidhin, khizy is genitive in annexation to day, and day is genitive before idh.
rows.anchor: فأضاف (خزي) الى "اليوم" فجره وأضاف "اليوم" الى "إذ" فجره

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read yawmaʾidhin in the accusative, treating the compound as one noun with inflection at its end.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم (يومئذ) فنصب لانه جعله اسما واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd is declined when understood as the people or their ancestor; the non-declined reading treats it as a feminine tribal name, but Akhfash reads the declined form and allows declension generally for a masculine people or ancestor name.
rows.anchor: وانما قرىء منه مصروفا ما كانت فيه الألف. وبذلك نقرأ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuduww denotes morning though it is morphologically a verb; ibkār derives from abkara, while some explain al-abkār as the plural of bakr.
rows.anchor: وقال {بالغدو والآصال} و {بالعشي والإبكار} فجعل "الغدو" يدل على الغداة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects pluralizing bakr as abkār because bakr is an indeclinable noun and a verbal noun like ibkār; the alternative claims the forms are plurals of bakra and ghudwa, but faʿla does not pluralize as afʿāl.
rows.anchor: لانه اسم ليس بمتمكن وهو أيضا مصدر مثل "الإبكار"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am here is the disconnected particle that begins a new question rather than coordinating with what precedes.
rows.anchor: وقال {أم جعلوا لله شركاء} فهذه "أم" التي تكون منقطعة من أول الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic has both qadr and qadar in expressions such as qadr/qadar shibr and qadartu aqdiru qadran; both vowelings also occur in the saying al-qadr.
rows.anchor: تقول: "أعطني قدر شبر" و"قدر شبر" وتقول: "قدرت" و"أنا أقدر"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is elliptical: from what they kindle for ornament or use comes foam like this foam.
rows.anchor: وقال {أو متاع زبد مثله} يقول: "ومن ذلك الذي يوقدون عليه زيد مثله"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salāmun ʿalaykum is direct speech from the angels, meaning they say, Peace be upon you.
rows.anchor: وقال {يدخلون عليهم من كل باب [23] سلام عليكم} أي: يقولون "سلام عليكم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khāliqīn means makers or craftsmen, which explains the expression aḥsanu al-khāliqīn; an unnamed poet uses khalaqa for making.
rows.anchor: وقال {أحسن الخالقين} لأن الخالقين هم الصانعون. وقال الشاعر: [من الكامل وهو الشاهد الثالث والخمسون بعد المئتين] : * وأراك تغري ماخلقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-shajaratan is coordinated with fa-anshaʾnā janāt, continuing the earlier statement about bringing forth gardens.
rows.anchor: وقال {وشجرة تخرج} على "فأنشأنا جنات" {وشجرة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna hādhihi ummatukum ummatan wāḥidatan has ummatan wāḥidatan as a circumstantial accusative; some read it as a nominative predicate in apposition.
rows.anchor: قال {وإن هاذه أمتكم أمة واحدة} فنصب {أمة واحدة} على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huma lahā sābiqūn means they hasten for the sake of those good deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال {هم لها سابقون} يقول: من أجلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in mā jaʿala Allāhu li-rajulin min qalbayni reinforces the negation; the sense is mā jaʿala li-rajulin qalbayni, as in raʾaytu Zaydan nafsahu.
rows.anchor: قال {من قلبين في جوفه} إنما هو "ما جعل الله لرجل قلبين في جوفه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition li- follows the passive idea because Arabic says huwa yudʿā li-fulān, he is called after so-and-so.
rows.anchor: وقال {ادعوهم لآبائهم} لأنك تقول "هو يدعى لفلان"

words: إِلَّا أَن تَفْعَلُوا إِلَىٰ أَوْلِيَائِكُم مَّعْرُوفًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illā an tafʿalū is accusative as an exception outside the main clause.
rows.anchor: وقال {إلا أن تفعلوا} في موضع نصب واستثناء خارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People's ṣalāh for the Prophet is their supplication for him, while God's ṣalāh is the spreading of good mention about him.
rows.anchor: وقال {إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي ياأيها الذين آمنوا صلوا عليه وسلموا تسليما} فصلاة الناس عليه دعاؤهم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illā qalīlan means they will not remain neighbors except briefly, with qalīlan functioning as a verbal noun for a short duration.
rows.anchor: {إلا قليلا} أي: "لا يجاورونك فيهآ إلا قليلا" على المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense is that intercession occurs only for someone whom God has permitted to be interceded for.
rows.anchor: وقال {لمن أذن له} لأن في المعنى لا يشفع الا لمن له أذن له*

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq may be read either in the nominative or the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقال {قالوا الحق} ان شئت رفعت وان شئت نصبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is not uncertainty: Arabic presents two sides while meaning that the speaker is guided; a master can say one of us is striking his companion and be understood as the striker.
rows.anchor: وقال {وإنآ أو إياكم لعلى هدى} فليس هذا لأنه شك ولكن هذا في كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording permits rajʿa ilayhi al-qawla, literally returning the speech to him, as an Arabic construction.
rows.anchor: وقال {يرجع بعضهم إلى بعض القول} لأنك تقول "قد رجعت إليه القول"
